input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives Sparkling an unconditional right to terminate the Agreement at any time on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, which sits squarely at the fallback notice window of 60–90 days. No early-termination fee, penalty or accelerated-payment mechanic attaches to that exit: Section 11 and the Fee Schedule reference only fees payable in the ordinary course, so the fallback cap of three months' fees is satisfied (in fact exceeded, at nil). On the Vendor side, Garman's only termination rights arise under Section 17(c) for insolvency events or an uncured material default; nothing anywhere in the document (including Sections 7, 8 and 10) gives Garman any right to terminate for convenience, so the fallback limits on Vendor convenience termination (end-of-term only, 90 days' notice) are met and the preferred element that Garman have no convenience right during a committed term is also satisfied. Falling short of the preferred position only in that notice is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a Sparkling convenience termination (a refund is provided only on Garman default under Section 17(c)); these are noted rather than redlined because the clause meets the fallback on its material terms. This sits at the fallback and we do not propose changes.
